system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A Kerberos ticket and successful RDP logon show omar.haddad connecting to WS-BCARTER-01 from 192.0.2.45. The inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-OHADDAD-01, and the environment has no VPN.

The domain account it_helper was created at 13:44:18 with omar.haddad recorded as the subject, then added to the Administrators group two seconds later. This conflicts with the stated practice that help-desk temporary accounts use tmp.<name> and never receive administrator rights.

A task named Microsoft\Windows\HealthCheck was registered under omar.haddad shortly afterward. It runs hidden PowerShell with an encoded command that decodes to downloading and executing a script from http://192.0.2.45/a.ps1.

The sequence of an unauthorized-source RDP session, creation of a new administrator account, and registration of a disguised task that downloads and executes a script is consistent with malicious activity.

A Commvault service started on WS-BCARTER-01 and attempted explicit authentication to FILE-HD-01 as svc-claimsync. The inventory describes ClaimSync as a FILE-HD-01 job and identifies CobaltVault, not Commvault, as the approved backup agent.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records do not show the process that performed the domain account creation or group addition.
The task registration is recorded, but the evidence does not show whether the task ran or whether its script was retrieved or executed.
The records do not establish who controlled the source address 192.0.2.45.
claims_not_established: Whether the RDP session, account changes, or task registration were authorized by the organization.
Whether it_helper was subsequently used to log on or access resources.
Whether the task's remote script was successfully downloaded or executed.
Whether the Commvault service and svc-claimsync authentication were related to the account creation or task.
additional_evidence_needed: Investigate and preserve WS-BCARTER-01, including the RDP session, task definition and execution history, PowerShell logs, and relevant process/network telemetry.
Review DC-HD-01 audit records and directory state to determine the source and scope of the account creation and Administrators-group change.
Identify and validate the owner and authorization for source address 192.0.2.45; review related firewall, proxy, and network records.
Review FILE-HD-01 and WS-BCARTER-01 service configuration and authentication logs for the Commvault process and svc-claimsync credentials.
